messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: gateway error rate spike detected. 5xx+timeouts rising rapidly for /v1/generate across all hosted clusters. Paging mira (oncall). Dashboard: https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/48912 :rotating_light:

mira (oncall): got it, looking. initial summary?

diego (sre): i'm seeing queue_depth for batcher-scheduler spike to 22k on eu-west-1, CPU on batcher nodes maxed, batcher accept rate dropped. TLDR: batcher saturation -> HOL blocking -> gateway timeouts.

sam (eng-runtime): logs show batcher scheduling backlog and a ton of "enqueue timeout". kv-cache size also increased, possibly blocking eviction paths. snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] batcher-scheduler ERROR enqueue timeout id=0x7f4 msg_count=64 wait_ms=1280
[2026-03-15T10:02:12Z] kvcache WARN eviction delayed size=1.2G
```

mira (oncall): customer impact? Sara can you pull CS triage numbers?

sara (customer-success): early signals: ~6% of API calls returning 5xx or timing out in last 10m. Several enterprise customers reported increased latency >20s, two reported timeouts in production. No major account outage yet but degraded. I'm pinging top 5 affected accounts and opening support threads.

kevin (frontend): we just flipped a feature flag that increased request pacing last hour in eu-west, could be correlated. Reverting now but traffic already spiked.

mira (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) throttle ingress to reduce batcher pressure 2) scale batcher pool 3) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant 4) clear kv-cache if stuck 5) if needed, route traffic to standby region. I'll try steps 1-3 now.

diego (sre): +1. I'll stand by for scaling and assist with cache eviction. Also prepare to disable long-batching policy (policy_v3).

sam (eng-runtime): commands I'll run: ```
# scale batcher workers in eu-west-1
rdwctl autoscale set --pool=batcher-eu-west --replicas=8 --force
# disable policy_v3 batching
rdwctl config apply --service=batcher --set batching.policy=policy_v2
```

mira (oncall): applying ingress throttle to API gateway: ```
# set token bucket to 80% of baseline for eu-west routes
gatewayctl rate-limit set --route "/v1/*" --region eu-west-1 --pct=80 --reason="emergency throttling - batcher saturation"
```

ops-bot: NOTE: throttle applied by mira (oncall). Alert updated: reduced incoming QPS by ~25% in eu-west.

diego (sre): starting batcher scale now. I'll also evict old kv entries to free up memory. ```
# force kv eviction on batcher nodes
rdwctl debug kv-evict --pool batcher-eu-west --age=1h
```

sam (eng-runtime): policy flip done. batcher replicas scaling... logs: ```
[2026-03-15T10:07:02Z] autoscaler INFO pool=batcher-eu-west target=8 status=starting
```

kevin (frontend): reverted request pacing flag. We should see inbound QPS drop over next minute.

mira (oncall): traffic drop observed. Error rate starting to decline from 6% -> 3.2%. Tail latencies still elevated but trending down. Monitoring shows head-of-line queue melting slowly.

sara (customer-success): updated affected customers. Two customers asked for ETA; I've told them we're actively mitigating and will follow up in 30m.

diego (sre): one deeper issue: scheduler's preemption path is stuck on a small subset of queues; restarting scheduler worker pod to restore fair-queuing. Doing rolling restart on batcher-scheduler-controllers. ```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/batcher-scheduler-controller -l region=eu-west-1
```

ops-bot: DEPLOY BOT: rollout restarted batcher-scheduler-controller (eu-west-1). Started at 2026-03-15T10:12:48Z.

sam (eng-runtime): restart completed, scheduler regained normal throughput. enqueue timeout logs reduced.

mira (oncall): current status: error rate 1.1%, gateway timeouts down to baseline. We still have some elevated latencies for long prompts; keep monitoring. Are we comfortable keeping throttle and scaled replicas?

diego (sre): keep both for 15-30m. I'll monitor queue_depth and KV eviction metrics. If stable for 30m, scale-down replicas and remove throttle.

sara (customer-success): customers informed of mitigation steps. No escalations at this time.

kevin (frontend): putting a temporary client-side retry window on web UI to avoid spamming API during this recovery.

mira (oncall): preparing handoff. I'm staying until metrics look green, but my shift ends at 10:45Z. diego, can you take over if it's not fully resolved?

diego (sre): I can take over. Oncall-next tagged. I'll keep the throttle for 20m and start a rolling scale-down if stable.

mira (oncall): Handoff notes for diego: root cause likely an interaction between recent client pacing change + aggressive batching policy that allowed large batch waits; combined with kv-cache growth causing eviction stalls -> scheduler backlog. Actions taken: ingress throttle, reverted client pacing flag, disabled policy_v3, scaled batcher to 8 replicas, forced kv eviction, restarted scheduler controllers. Customer impact: ~6% 5xx at peak, reduced to ~1% now. Follow-ups: postmortem to include detailed timeline, load test for policy_v3 scenario, add automatic preemption when queue_depth > 10k, and add a runbook step to auto-failover to smaller model variant on queued-latency spike.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced. Incident channel lock set to read-only for 10m while next-oncall performs validation.

oncall-next: acknowledged, taking over. I'll check back in at 10:30Z with status and start post-incident doc if stable.

mira (oncall): signing off to rest. Leaving pinned mitigation state in the console. Good job everyone. :heart:

diego (sre): thanks team. I'll watch the metrics and start a short postmortem draft once we confirm full recovery.
